conditions.manipulation_text: Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A separator overfilled; liquid entered the gas line and treatment unit, damaged the unit generators, shut down the unit, and caused production loss. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

surface_forms.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

case_payload.task: Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
case_payload.title: Comprehensive Node 1 HAZOP after a salient vessel-overfill incident vignette

surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 consists of FWKO three-phase separator V-001, heat exchanger E-001, and associated piping and instrumentation operating nominally at 60 psig and 130 °F, bounded by design limits of 125 psig and 200 °F. Systematic HAZOP analysis identifies critical physical deviations in pressure (gas blockage / vessel overpressure), level (liquid carryover to fuel gas/burn pit or gas blowby to downstream Heater-Treater and water treatment), flow, temperature, and corrosion. Additionally, a human-procedural deviation is identified regarding unit start-up without bypass opening based on source data. Safeguards include PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, LV-101/102, SDVs, and alarms.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Reverse Flow in Node 1 process lines (unresolved: check valve specifications and hydraulic elevations are not documented in the system packet)
Internal Fire/Explosion inside V-001 (non-applicable: the vessel operates as a closed hydrocarbon system devoid of internal oxygen under normal operating conditions)
Organizational factor deviations (non-applicable / excluded: packet SYS-09 mandates no invention of organizational facts)

consequences: Vessel overpressure exceeding nominal 60 psig towards design limit of 125 psig
Potential challenge to containment integrity if relief system fails

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal operating pressure of 60 psig and upper condition of 125 psig.
Describes gas discharge routing to fuel gas and burn pit.
Identifies PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, PIT-101, and SDV-30010 as Node 1 components.

possible_causes: Spurious closure or failure of PV-101 pressure control loop
Blockage or restriction in gas line to fuel gas system or burn pit
Excess gas surge in inlet crude stream
recommendations: Verify that PSV-101 A/B sizing is validated for full blocked outlet capacity under maximum design conditions (125 psig and 200 °F)
Ensure high-pressure trip from PIT-101 automatically closes SDV-30010

consequences: Liquid carryover into separated gas line
Contamination of fuel gas network or liquid discharge into burn pit posing safety and environmental hazards

evidence.relevance: Establishes three-phase separation mechanism for oil, gas, and free water.
Documents separated gas destination to fuel gas and burn pit.
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102.

possible_causes: Failure closed or throttling of LV-101 (oil) or LV-102 (water) control valves
Downstream line blockage towards Heater-Treater or water treatment
Sudden slug of liquid entering V-001
recommendations: Confirm high-liquid-level alarms on V-001 and interlock high-high level to isolate feed via SDV-30010
Verify fuel gas knock-out provisions downstream

consequences: Gas blowby through liquid outlets into downstream Heater-Treater or water treatment facilities

evidence.relevance: Describes downstream flow path to Heater-Treater separator.
Describes water routing to water treatment.
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102.

existing_safeguards: LV-101 and LV-102 level control loops
possible_causes: Failure open of LV-101 or LV-102 control valves
Loss of liquid feed with outlet valves remaining open
recommendations: Verify low-low liquid level interlocks on V-001 that immediately trip closed SDV-101 and SDV-102
Ensure downstream systems have appropriate relief protection against gas blowby

consequences: Starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and Desalter units
Thermal imbalance or stagnant fluid overheating in E-001

evidence.relevance: Details continuous process sequence through V-001, Heater-Treater, and V-003 Desalter.
Specifies E-001, SDV-30010, FIT-101, and FAL-103.

possible_causes: Spurious trip or closure of SDV-30010
Upstream production well shutdown or pipeline blockage
Severe fouling or plugging in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Confirm FAL-103 triggers operational alerts to adjust upstream/downstream heating and separation operations safely

consequences: Operating temperature exceeding nominal 130 °F towards upper envelope limit of 200 °F
Increased vapor generation and potential flash separation disturbances in V-001

evidence.relevance: Sets nominal temperature at 130 °F and upper operating text limit at 200 °F.
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as associated Node 1 equipment.

existing_safeguards: Temperature monitoring within published 130 °F to 200 °F operating limits
possible_causes: Excessive heating in upstream E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Higher temperature feed from upstream production source
recommendations: Verify temperature measurement and high-temperature alarms at the outlet of E-001 to prevent thermal runaway above 200 °F

consequences: Deadheading of inlet feed line or transient pressure surges in V-001
Premature actuation or lifting of PSV-101 A/B and potential SDV trip during commissioning

evidence.relevance: Includes Start/Stop Procedures as a required study element.
Explicitly highlights source-supported procedural deviation concerning FWKO start-up without bypass opening.

possible_causes: Procedural non-compliance or omission during FWKO start-up sequence
Lack of explicit verification step or checklist for bypass alignment prior to introducing feed
recommendations: Update standard operating procedures (SOPs) for V-001 start-up to mandate a hold point and verification checklist for bypass opening
Provide operator training specifically addressing FWKO start-up sequencing

consequences: Degradation and wall thinning of V-001 vessel shell, lower boot, and water outlet line
Loss of primary containment if degradation is undetected

evidence.relevance: Identifies free water separation based on density differences.
Identifies water discharge line to water treatment.
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as an analysis element.

existing_safeguards: Continuous water discharge control via LV-102 preventing stagnant accumulation
Vessel design allowance and PSV-101 A/B for overpressure protection
possible_causes: Corrosive species and brine in separated free water settling in separator vessel
Sand and abrasive solids carried over from crude production stream
recommendations: Establish periodic non-destructive ultrasonic thickness testing and corrosion monitoring on V-001 boot and bottom piping

uncertainty_notes: Specific trip setpoints and interlock logics connecting PIT-101 to SDV-30010 and level instrumentation to SDV-101/102 are not specified in the packet.
Piping layout details and the presence of check valves to evaluate reverse flow are omitted from the system documentation.
Exchanger heating medium parameters and controls for E-001 are not documented.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LEVEL-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
